passage:
The city replaced some old benches with new ones that had metal bars between seats. Officials said the design stopped people from sleeping there.
A student group questioned the decision. They said public spaces should be comfortable for everyone, including people without homes.
The class discussed design ethics. A bench is not just a bench if its shape decides who is welcome.
Some students argued that parks need order. Others said solving homelessness by making rest uncomfortable was not a real solution.
The debate changed how students saw ordinary objects.
Design can be quiet, but it has power. It can invite, guide, limit, or exclude.
